content:
tara: Heads-up — hit a weird tree-shaking / default-import interop when bundling the JS SDK for edge functions (Cloudflare/Netlify). It strips our auth registration side-effect on some build paths. Repro below.

tara: Repro steps (minimal):
```bash
mkdir sdk-repro && cd sdk-repro
npm init -y
# using esbuild/vite/rollup combos we use in sampleapps
npm i vite rollup esbuild --save-dev
npm i ../local-packages/redwood-inference
# create simple handler and build for edge target
```

tara: handler.mjs:
```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'
// SDK registers auth on import side-effect: registerAuth()
const c = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY })
export default async function (req) {
  const res = await c.generate('hi')
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res))
}
```

tara: Build with vite (target=es2020, build.lib: formats=["es"], ssr:false) or rollup with commonjs plugin + esbuild. On deploy to a Netlify edge function we get: 
```
Error: Unauthorized: missing api key
    at registerRequest (runtime:/layers/edge/handler.js:45:12)
```
tara: Local inspection shows SDK's import-side registerAuth() never executed when bundler inlined and collapsed the default import into the constructor function.

nina: Can you paste package.json inside node_modules/redwood-inference? suspect exports/sideEffects settings.

tara: package.json excerpt: 
```json
{"name":"redwood-inference","main":"dist/index.cjs.js","module":"dist/index.esm.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts","sideEffects":false,"exports":{".":{"require":"./dist/index.cjs.js","import":"./dist/index.esm.js"}}}
```

tara: Note: sideEffects:false at package level. Our SDK relies on import-time side-effects to wire up auth adapters (we register a global fetch hook on import). With sideEffects:false, bundlers consider the module tree-shakable and may drop the import if the export shapes are inlined. That explains why some bundlers remove the module init.

oscar: Ah — explicit bug. Two PR-level options: 1) set sideEffects: true for dist files that run side-effects, or 2) split side-effect-only entry (e.g., "./dist/setup.js") and document importing it. Both are valid.

nina: Also happened with TS typings: editor auto-imports prefer default import, which then gets inlined by bundler. Typings look okay but moduleResolution: bundler resolves to CJS in some envs.

tara: Quick temporary fixes:
- In onboarding sample apps, include `import 'redwood-inference/setup'` or `import { registerAuth } from 'redwood-inference'` before using Client.
- Change examples to use `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` which seems to preserve the import so side-effect stays.

oscar: Long-term: update build pipeline to emit a tiny side-effect entry and set package.json sideEffects array to include that file. E.g. "sideEffects": ["./dist/register-auth.js"]. Also update publishing to ensure CJS sets module.exports.default = module.exports for safer default import interop.

buildkite: Created ticket RD-4021: "Bundlers strip SDK import side-effects with sideEffects:false causing auth registration to drop". Assigned to eng-devex.

tara: I'll make a quick PR to change package.json sideEffects and add a setup import in the sampleapp templates + a short note in onboarding docs advising explicit import until fixed.

nina: Good plan. Also add a short repro repository under examples/edge-bundler-sideeffect so folks can reproduce with Vite/Rollup/Netlify. Keep the repro minimal.

tara: Will do. For anyone hitting 401s in edge builds, check: 1) do you rely on SDK import side-effects? 2) does your bundler treat the SDK as side-effect-free? Workaround snippet: 
```js
// ensure init runs
import 'redwood-inference/register'
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: ... })
```
devx-bot: Linked ticket RD-4021 and added label: "dx:blocker".

tara: Thanks — will follow up with PR numbers and sample app link.
